title: What's Inside Counts: Why Trims Matter for Fashion's Environmental Impact
text:
For Hong Kong-based pocketing and lining manufacturer Sungil Tex, the answer to reducing the impact of these inner textiles lies in biodegradability.
Successfully producing a sustainable garment comes down to the details. Along with curating the material composition of outer layers, product developers should be looking closely at alland lining manufacturer Sungil Tex, the answer to reducing the impact of these inner textiles lies in biodegradability.
Here, the company’s chief executive officer Danny Lee discusses how Sungil Tex is designing for products’ end of life, why biodegradability matters inSOURCING JOURNAL: More attention is being placed on the long-term impacts of textile waste, including the persistence of fabrics in landfills and water. Nonbiodegradable linings turn the end-of-life disposal into a complex, costly and time-consuming problem, as the garment cannot decompose fully. To achieve true circularity and eliminate the long-term impacts of textile waste in landfills and oceans, every single component—down to the hiddenlinings and pocketings. We adopted Tencel Lyocell, EcoVero Viscose and Naia, which align perfectly with this mission. These specific fibers are manufactured using environmentally responsible production processes and are scientifically proven to be biodegradable.
By integrating these premium yarns into our collections, we ensure that our linings not only offer exceptional quality and an elegant drape but also return safely to nature at the end of their life cycle. Everyday consumers—and even industry professionals—cannot determine the environmental footprint or authenticity of a lining simply by looking at or touching it. In an era where “greenwashing” is a valid concern, words are no longer enough.
Certifications are absolutely critical because they provide undeniable, third-party verification of our sustainability claims. They offer complete transparency, giving our brand partners the confidence they need to market their garments truthfully, and ultimately giving end consumers the trust they deserve when purchasing eco-friendly fashion. One hurdle the industry faces in tackling waste is having to reach high minimum order quantities. Why has Sungil Tex opted to mostly eliminate MOQs?
When we first introduced our biodegradable linings two to three years ago, we noticed that high MOQs and long lead times prevented brands from adopting these sustainable options across their entire collections. We realized that to truly drive industry-wide change, we had to lower the barrier to entry. To make this viable, we analyzed market data to identify the most frequently used colors.
By proactively producing and maintaining optimal stock levels of these core colors, we can offer a “No MOQ” service. This operational shift empowers more clients to seamlessly integrate biodegradable linings into a wider range of styles. Synthetics are still sought-after for certain programs. How have you worked to reduce the impact of these fabrics to keep them as a viable option?
Certain performance characteristics sometimes necessitate the use of synthetic linings for durability and function. Instead of ignoring this need, we are actively innovating to bridge the gap between performance and sustainability. Sungil Tex is in the advanced stages of developing a cutting-edge biodegradable polyester lining, specifically engineered to meet the rigorous standards of European luxury menswear brands. This allows us to deliver the high performance of synthetics without compromising our commitment to reducing long-term environmental impact.
Realistically, cost remains a significant barrier. Because linings are considered “hidden” trims, many brands still prioritize price over sustainability when sourcing them.
However, we are witnessing a promising shift. Leading luxury fashion houses and dedicated sustainable brands are increasingly driving the demand for eco-friendly trims. They recognize that true luxury today means sustainability down to the smallest detail. As consumer awareness grows, we expect this trend to trickle down into broader markets, eventually making sustainable linings the industry standard rather than an optional upgrade.
